summary: The bill amends the National Housing Act and related laws to let state-licensed appraisers conduct FHA mortgage appraisals if they meet Uniform Standards competency rules plus FHA-specific education, adds trainee appraisers to the national registry and allows them to assist certified appraisers, authorizes registry fee adjustments and workforce training grants, and adds HUD, VA, and USDA to the Appraisal Subcommittee.

scores.thoughts: Section 5 of the bill amends existing law to authorize grants from the Appraisal Subcommittee to state agencies, nonprofits, and higher education institutions specifically for appraiser workforce education, training, recruitment, scholarships, and career pipelines. This constitutes a new federal grant program, which would expand government spending, albeit in a narrow and targeted way.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses FHA mortgage appraisal standards and the appraiser workforce; it has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No provisions address firearms, gun ownership, or related regulations.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or related healthcare regulations.
No provisions address military, defense, or national security spending or policy.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resource management.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other safety-net programs.

Section 5 authorizes grants that may support education and training activities for appraisers, but these are narrowly targeted professional workforce grants rather than general public education, K-12 schooling, or school-choice policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill authorizes a modest new grant program but does not contain any debt-reduction measures, deficit targets, or fiscal rules.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections, nondiscrimination rules, or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international aid, or development funding.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter ID requirements.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address union rights, collective bargaining, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and antidiscrimination rules.
